answer.location_description: A thin horizontal band spanning the full image width at rows 2-3, near the top edge, well above the nodule. Weaker, similar full-width bands appear near the bottom (rows 18-19 and 22-23).
answer.shortcut_type: full-width horizontal bright line/band artifact near top edge
answer.mechanism: About 14 first-layer units (0, 3, 5, 12, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24, 28) have uniform positive weights (about +40 to +65) across all 24 columns of rows 2-3. These units feed layer-2 units u9 (W3 -95) and u12 (W3 -63), which push the logit toward benign. The malignant-side units 9, 16 and 30 have uniformly negative weights on rows 2-3 and feed u2 (+99) and u4 (+93). They are also inhibited in u2 by units 3, 5, 13, 21 and 23. So a bright line at rows 2-3 raises the benign pathway and suppresses the malignant pathway.
answer.evidence: Rows 2-3 carry the most uniform, column-independent weights in the network. Examples: unit 3 r2 = 21..60 everywhere, unit 14 r3 up to 65, unit 18 r3 up to 70, unit 19 r2-r3 = 19..64. There are sharp transitions to near-zero or mixed weights at rows 0-1 and row 4. Units 9, 16 and 30 show the mirror image: r2-r3 about -20 to -59, with r4-r5 positive. A centered-nodule feature would be roughly radially symmetric, not a straight full-width stripe at the image edge. Several layer-2 couplings are among the largest in their rows: u9 takes +95, +95 and +91 from units 13, 14 and 23; u2 takes +93 from unit 30. Similar but less clean full-width bands at rows 18-19 and 22-23 may belong to the same artifact pattern.
answer.main_feature: Nodule size and shape. A small, compact bright center (rows 10-12, cols 10-13) surrounded by a dark lung ring drives the benign units. A broad bright mass filling a large region around the center (rows 4-17), as detected by units 9, 16 and 30 and by unit 27's overall-brightness detector, drives the malignant output.
